A request that changes nothing answers `unchanged` and writes nothing, so retrying after a timeout is safe. The product comes back with `write_result`. Send `If-None-Match: *` to create only.

parameters.description: Deprecated: send an `external_id`, which makes a retry an update of the product the first call created. Without an `external_id`, a retry with the same key returns the originally created product instead of creating a duplicate. With an `external_id` the header is ignored.

Ids generated for a new product, its features and usage prices, and `write_result.price_version.new_price_id` are never stored: a `GET` of them answers `404`. A `meter_external_id` that names no meter is a `reference_not_found` warning (`path`, `key`) instead of a `400`: on a create that usage price is left out of the answer, and on an update of an existing product the stored usage prices stay as they are. `false` or no parameter is a real call; any other value answers `400`.

post.description:

Returns **202 Accepted** with the number of events accepted and the `event_id` of each, in submission order — your own value where you supplied one, a generated value where you did not.

Ingestion is **idempotent on (store, event_id)**: re-sending an event_id this store has already accepted records nothing and is not an error, so **retrying a whole batch after a timeout or a partial failure is always safe**. Duplicates are deduplicated silently rather than reported — a replayed batch returns the same 202 and the same `event_ids` as the original. Supply your own `event_id` to get that guarantee; when you omit it we generate one, which makes the event unique and a retry a second event.

Your `event_id` is **stored trimmed**, and the `event_ids` we return are the stored values — so `" abc "` is recorded and echoed as `"abc"`, which is what `reference=` on `GET /v1/events` matches. Two entries in one batch whose ids differ only by surrounding whitespace are therefore the **same** event: the second is deduplicated against the first, both are reported accepted, and both carry the same id. An `event_id` that is entirely whitespace is rejected like an empty one (422) rather than being replaced with a generated id — an unusable key is worth telling you about.

The **whole batch is validated before anything is accepted**: if any event is invalid the request is rejected with 422 and `param` pointing at the offending event (e.g. `events[3].customer_id`), and no event in the batch is ingested.

Billing attribution uses the `timestamp` you supply (defaulting to the time of ingestion), bounded by the late-event window: once a billing period has been closed for longer than that window, an event arriving for it is still stored durably but is no longer folded into that period's totals.

**202, not 200, is deliberate.** It means the batch has been accepted for processing, not that every downstream effect has completed: aggregation into meter totals is already asynchronous today, and the transport behind this endpoint may become queue-backed. A queue producer cannot know how many rows a consumer will ultimately insert, so this response reports acceptance rather than an insert/duplicate split — the contract you code against stays identical when that lands.

post.summary: Validate a batch of catalog writes together, without writing anything.
post.description: Runs every item as its own write would run with `?dry_run=true`, but all of them in one database transaction that is always rolled back, so the batch is checked as a whole: an item may name a resource another item of the batch creates (a product's usage price naming a new meter by `meter_external_id`), and every check, uniqueness rule and guard runs against what the earlier items would have written. Items run in dependency order (meters, products, product groups, discounts) and are answered in the order of the request. Without `id` an item runs as the keyed upsert of its kind (`POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/meters`) with the same body; with `id` it runs as that resource's `PATCH` with `PATCH`'s rules, which is meant for a migrator adopting an existing resource (giving it an `external_id`). Requires `products:write` and the write scope of every kind in the batch (`meters:write` for meters). Nothing is written and nothing is triggered. A batch that passes can still fail when it is applied, if the catalog changes in between; validate it again right before applying it.

200.description: Every item passes. One answer per item, in the order of the request.

400.description: Bad request, and nothing was checked. Besides validation errors of the request itself: `validate_batch_too_large`: the batch holds more than 100 items (`details.max_items`, `details.items`); split it, for example one dependency layer per call. `dry_run_not_supported`: an item's `kind` can't be validated yet (`details.kind`: `product_group` or `discount`), or the request sent `dry_run` (validate never writes). `validate_batch_timeout`: the batch couldn't be checked within 15 seconds (`details.timeout_ms`), because its items are large or one waited on a resource another request was writing; nothing was written. Split it into smaller batches; sending the same batch again takes as long. An item's own validation error is not a `400` of the call: it is that item's answer in a `422`.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing API key

403.description: Forbidden: the API key or access token lacks `products:write` or the write scope of a kind in the batch (`meters:write`, `discounts:write`). Nothing was checked.

404.description: Not Found - Resource does not exist

422.description: At least one item fails. The same answer as `200`, with `valid` `false`: each failing item carries its endpoint’s status and error body. Nothing was written.

post.summary: Promote the test catalog to live (meters and products).
post.description:
Copies the store’s test catalog into live by `external_id`: each selected test item is matched to the live item with the same key and written as that kind’s keyed upsert (`POST /v1/meters`, `POST /v1/products`); a keyed test item without a live match is created with its key. Test is the source for every field it sets; promote never clears a `metadata` key only live has (`conflict`), and live items without a test counterpart are not listed and never touched. A test item without a key is `needs_key`, with ranked `candidates` and a `proposed_external_id`: give both sides the same key, then promote again. Archived test items are included only when live has an item with the same key, and a paired meter’s archive state follows test’s.

Every item reports one `result`; the real run writes only `created`, `updated` and `unchanged` items. Before its first write the real run checks every write together in one rolled-back transaction (one dependency layer at a time above the batch limit) and writes nothing when one fails, unless `force` is `true`. The check runs within the time budget too: until it is done a page has no items and a `next_cursor`, and `validation.checked_batches` says how far it got. Then the run writes only what it checked: an item changed after the check is `not_written` (`changed_since_check`). Items run meters first, then products, then the meters test archived (a meter's archive is part of its own write, after the products that may stop pricing it), and pages end after a time budget: follow `next_cursor` with the same `select` and `dry_run` until it is null. Every run and item is recorded under `run_id`, dry runs included.

Requires `products:write` and `meters:write` when meters are promoted. Answers `503` `test_environment_unavailable` when the test environment can’t be reached; try again later.

parameters.name: dry_run
parameters.description: Send `true` to preview: every item runs as its upsert’s dry run and is rolled back, so nothing is written in live (no row, no event, no Stripe call). The answer has the same shape as the real run’s, with `write_result.dry_run` `true`. Page a dry run with `cursor` like a real run.

200.description: The page’s items, also when some of them are `conflict`, `failed` or `blocked`.

400.description: Bad request, and nothing ran. Besides validation errors of the request: `live_only`: called on the test API (promote runs on live); `reference_not_found`: a test id in `select` the test store doesn’t have (`details.field`, `details.key`); `invalid_cursor`: a cursor not issued for this `select` and `dry_run`, or older than 24 hours.

401.description: Unauthorized - Invalid or missing API key

403.description: Forbidden: the API key or access token lacks `products:write`, or `meters:write` for a selection with meters. Nothing was read or written.

404.description: Not Found - Resource does not exist

503.description: Service unavailable (`test_environment_unavailable`): the test environment can’t be reached. Nothing was written; try again later.

info.title: Creem API
info.description: Creem is an all-in-one platform for managing subscriptions and recurring revenue, tailored specifically for today's SaaS companies. It enables you to boost revenue, enhance customer retention, and scale your operations seamlessly.

servers.description: Production — live API for processing real transactions and data.
Test — sandbox API for development and testing with no real charges.

ApiKey.name: x-api-key
ApiKey.description: API key for authentication. You can find your API key in the Creem dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

ProductStatus.description: Lifecycle status of the product: `active` or `archived`.

ProductFeatureType.description: The type of the feature: `custom` (private note), `file` (downloadable files), `licenseKey` (license key), `customerCredits` (customer credit grant), or `githubRepository` (access to a private GitHub repository).

amount.description: The number of credits to grant. String to preserve BigInt precision.

unit_label.description: Optional label for the credit unit (e.g. "tokens", "credits").

bucket_name.description: The customer-credit bucket this grant funds — the `name` of the customer's credit account. Set it to a meter bucket (e.g. "images") so the credits fund a per-unit metered price; otherwise they land in `default` and metered usage cannot spend them. Distinct from `unit_label`, which is only a display label. On UPDATE the field is tri-state: OMIT it to leave the stored bucket unchanged, send `null` to clear it to the shared `default` wallet, or send a name to set it. On CREATE, omitted or null both mean `default`. A present-but-blank value is rejected.

requires_moderation.description: When `true`, the credits go to the customer's AI generation wallet: spending them requires a `moderation_id` from the Moderation API. `bucket_name` must be omitted (422 `bucket_name_not_allowed_with_requires_moderation`); that wallet is the reserved `generation` bucket. `generation` and `generation:*` (any casing) cannot be named directly (422 `generation_bucket_reserved`). Defaults to `false` on create; on update, omitting it keeps the stored setting, also when `bucket_name` is sent as `null` (as reads return it); send `false` to move the credits to the shared wallet, or to the `bucket_name` sent with it. Always present on reads.

resets_each_period.description: Unused credits from subscription grants expire at each renewal; credits from one-time purchases never expire. The reset runs on every paid subscription transaction of the product: renewals, and also the first paid charge after a trial and plan changes charged immediately. Each time, the part of the previous grant the customer did not spend expires before the new grant lands. Subscription products only (422 `credits_reset_requires_subscription` on a one-time product). Defaults to `false` on create. On update, omitting it keeps the stored setting only when the feature's `id` is sent; a feature sent without `id` is replaced and defaults to `false`. Always present on reads.

LicenseKeyExpiryInterval.description: The unit of the license key validity period.

interval_count.description: How many `interval`s a license key stays valid after it is issued.

activation_limit.description: How many devices or instances one license key can be activated on. `null` for unlimited activations; `0` for keys that can't be activated at all. On a write, `0` only when sending back a stored feature whose limit is `0`; anywhere else it answers `400`. The limit is checked at each activation, so a change applies to keys already issued too: activations they already have stay, and a key at or above a lowered limit can't be activated again.

expiry.description: How long a license key stays valid after it is issued. `null` for keys that never expire. Each key keeps the expiry it was issued with, so a change applies only to keys issued later.

file_name.description: The name buyers download the file under.

type.description: The MIME type of the file.

size.description: The size of the file in bytes.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of the file, base64-encoded, as `POST /v1/files/{id}/confirm` returns it. Compare it before uploading a file again. `null` for a file stored without one.

files.description: The files buyers can download after purchase.

description.description: A brief description of the feature.

external_id.description: Your own key for this feature, unique per product. `null` when the feature has none.

customer_credits.description: The credit grant behind a `customerCredits` feature. Absent for other feature types.

license_key.description: The settings of a `licenseKey` feature. Absent for other feature types.

private_note.description: The private note of a `custom` feature, shown to the customer after purchase. Absent for other feature types.
private_note.example: Thanks for your purchase! Your access code is XYZ123.

file.description: The files of a `file` feature, without their download links (buyers get those after purchase). Absent for other feature types.

UsagePriceSettlementMode.description: How the charge settles: `prepaid` debits the customer credit account as usage aggregates; `postpaid` bills at renewal where the store supports it.

UsagePriceTargetAccount.description: Credit bucket a prepaid charge debits: `shared` (the customer default wallet) or `per_unit` (a bucket named after the meter unit label, or `target_account_name`). Defaults to `shared`.

UsagePriceTrialUsageMode.description: Usage metered during a free trial: `free` is not charged, `accrue` is charged when the trial converts. Defaults to `free`.

id.description: Unique identifier of the usage price.

unit_price.description: Tax-exclusive price per SINGLE meter unit, in minor units of the product currency. "$20 per 1,000,000 tokens" is 0.002 (2000 cents / 1,000,000). Fractional values are allowed.

free_allowance.description: Meter units free per billing period, per customer, before the charge applies.

cap.description: Optional ceiling on the charge per billing period, in minor units. Null means uncapped.

target_account_name.description: The per-unit bucket this charge debits: the name given on write, or the meter unit label when none was. Null for a `shared` charge.

ProductBillingType.description: Indicates the billing method for the customer. It can either be a `recurring` billing cycle or a `onetime` payment.

TaxMode.description: Specifies the tax calculation mode for the transaction. If set to "inclusive," the tax is included in the price. If set to "exclusive," the tax is added on top of the price.

TaxCategory.description: Categorizes the type of product or service for tax purposes. This helps determine the applicable tax rules based on the nature of the item or service.

minimum_length.description: Minimum character length requirement for the input.

optional.description: Whether the customer is required to complete the field. Defaults to `false`.

image_urls.description: Ordered list of product image URLs. The first entry is the cover image (mirrored in image_url).

usage_prices.description: Metered charges billed on top of the base price, one per meter. Present on recurring products that meter usage.

price.description: The price of the product in cents. 1000 = $10.00

currency.description: Three-letter ISO currency code, in uppercase. Must be a supported currency.

recurring_interval.description: The unit of the recurring billing interval (`day`, `week`, `month`, or `year`). Together with `recurring_interval_count` this is authoritative for renewal timing — a `billing_period` of `custom` cannot be interpreted without it. For presets it is derived from the cadence (e.g. `every-three-months` → `month`). `null` for one-time products.

recurring_interval_count.description: The number of `recurring_interval` units per billing cycle (e.g. `3` with a `month` interval bills every three months). trial_period_days.description: Length of the trial period in days. A whole number of days, at least 1. Only supported for recurring products. `null` when the product has no trial.

trial_price.description: Amount charged at checkout to start the trial, instead of a free card verification. In cents (100 = $1.00). Requires a trial period and must be at least 100 and lower than `price`; only supported on standard-priced recurring products without pay-what-you-want. `null` for a free trial and for products without a trial.

pay_what_you_want.description: Whether buyers choose the amount they pay, at least `price`. One-time products only. Can be missing on a product embedded in another object.

suggested_price.description: The amount in cents pre-filled at checkout while `pay_what_you_want` is `true`; `null` when there is none. Checkout ignores it while `pay_what_you_want` is `false`. Can be missing on a product embedded in another object.

business_net_pricing.description: When true, business customers whose valid VAT ID triggers reverse charge pay the price excluding VAT instead of the tax-inclusive price. Only supported for tax-inclusive one-time products; the merchant gives up the VAT portion on those sales. Defaults to false.

product_url.description: The product page you can redirect your customers to for express checkout.

default_success_url.description: The URL to which the user will be redirected after successfull payment.

features.description: Features granted by purchase: `customerCredits` (a credit grant into one of the customer credit buckets), `licenseKey` (a license key per purchased unit), `custom` (a private note) and `file` (files buyers download, named by the ids of confirmed uploads from `POST /v1/files`). Omit (or send `null`) to leave features untouched. Otherwise the request replaces only the feature types it contains: for each of them, the entries are the complete set of that type after the update. Include `id` to edit in place, or the `external_id` of a stored feature to edit that feature without its `id`; features of that type missing from the array are removed. Types the array does not contain stay as they are, and `[]` removes the credit features and nothing else. An entry with `deleted: true` removes the one feature it names by `id` or `external_id`; it is the only way to remove the last feature of a type. Each refusal changes nothing: `400` `feature_type_mismatch` (an `id` or `external_id` of a feature of another type), `400` `feature_not_found` (an `id`, or a deletion, that names no feature of the product), `400` `feature_type_not_writable` (a `githubRepository` entry or deletion; those are managed in the dashboard), `400` `reference_not_found` (a file id that is unknown, of another store, or of an upload that was never confirmed), `400` `file_location_invalid` (a file of the store that is not stored under its own product-file key), and `409` `license_keys_issued` (removing a license-key feature whose keys customers hold; `details.issued_keys` counts them). Editing a license-key feature in place keeps its issued keys: a new `activation_limit` applies to them at once, a new `expiry` only to keys issued later. Removing a `file` feature, or a file from it, removes the download for every past buyer, as in the dashboard; adding it again restores it.

Trimmed; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.` and `:` only; at most 255 characters.

external_customer_id.description: Your own id for this customer, resolved to the Creem customer it was registered for via the customers API. event_id.description: Your idempotency key for this event, unique within your store. Re-sending the same event_id is a no-op. Generated for you when omitted — supply your own if you want retries to be safe.

timestamp.description: When the usage occurred (ISO 8601), on your clock. Defaults to the time of ingestion.

properties.description: The event's attributes — the ONE bag. Meter filter clauses and aggregation properties (e.g. "tokens") resolve their keys here, unprefixed. code.description: Warning code. `no_matching_meter`: no meter consumes this event name. `meter_archived`: only archived meters match — unarchive one to resume aggregation. `timestamp_outside_late_window`: the billing period the timestamp falls in is finalized, so the event will never change its totals.

kind.description: The kind of resource the item writes. `meter` and `product` can be validated; `product_group` and `discount` answer `400` `dry_run_not_supported` until their writes support a dry run.

id.description: For a migrator adopting an existing resource only: the id of the resource the item updates. With `id` the item runs as that resource’s `PATCH` (`PATCH /v1/products/{id}`, `PATCH /v1/meters/{id}`) with `PATCH`’s rules, for example to give a product without an `external_id` its key. Without `id` the item runs as the keyed upsert of its kind (`POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/meters`).

body.description: The request body of the write: without `id` the body of the kind’s create or upsert (`POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/meters`), with `id` the body of its `PATCH`. It is validated as that endpoint validates it.

items.description: The writes to check together, at most 100. They run in dependency order (meters, products, product groups, discounts), so an item may name a resource another item of the batch creates (a usage price's `meter_external_id`). A larger batch answers `400` `validate_batch_too_large` and nothing is checked.

id.description: The item’s `id`, or null for an upsert item.

valid.description: Whether the item’s write would succeed.

status.description: The status the item’s own endpoint answers for this write: `200` or `201` when it passes, its error status (`400`, `404`, `409`, `412`, `422`, …) when it fails.

response.description: When the item passes: what its endpoint answers with `?dry_run=true`, the resource with `write_result` (`dry_run` `true`), for a product the `POST` or `PATCH /v1/products` response, for a meter the `POST` or `PATCH /v1/meters` response. Ids of resources the batch would create are never stored. Null when the item fails.

error.description: When the item fails: the error body its endpoint answers, in that endpoint’s envelope, with its stable `code` (for example `external_id_taken`, `usage_price_in_use`, `meter_name_taken`). Null when the item passes.

valid.description: Whether every item passes. The status is `200` when it is true and `422` otherwise.

items.description: One entry per item, in the order of the request.

meters.description: `"all"` for every test meter, or a list of test meter ids. Leave it out to promote no meters (a product’s meters are still read to resolve its usage prices).

products.description: `"all"` for every test product, or a list of test product ids. Leave it out to promote no products.

select.description: What to promote, per kind (`meters`, `products`; product groups and discounts come later): `"all"` or a list of **test** ids. Omit `select` to promote everything; a kind left out of a sent `select` is not promoted. A test id the test store doesn’t have answers `400` `reference_not_found` (`details.field`, `details.key`) before anything runs.

cursor.description: Null (or omitted) on a run’s first call, then the `next_cursor` of the previous answer, with the same `select` and the same `dry_run`. A cursor is valid for 24 hours; any other cursor answers `400` `invalid_cursor`.

force.description: Real run only. Before its first write, promote checks every write of the selection together in one rolled-back transaction; when one fails, nothing is written and the answer’s `validation.written` is `false`. Send `true` to write anyway: each write still runs its own checks, and an item whose write is refused is a `conflict` or `failed` item. Defaults to `false`.

external_id.description: The live item’s `external_id`: the key to propose when the merchant picks this candidate. Null when it has none (then the test item’s id is proposed).

differences.description: The fields that differ from the test item (products: `price`, `currency`, `billing_type`, `billing_period`, `status`; meters: `event_name`, `aggregation`, `unit_label`, `status`). Shown, never matched on.

proposed_external_id.description: The key to write on both features: the test feature’s own `external_id` when it has one, else the picked live feature’s `external_id` when it has one, else the test feature’s id.

candidates.description: Live features of the same type nothing else matched; may be empty.

status.description: The status the item’s own write answers (`409` for a guard).

code.description: The stable error code, for example `usage_price_in_use`, `license_keys_issued`, `meter_in_use`, `live_metadata_not_in_test`, `reference_not_found`, `file_location_invalid`. More codes may be added.

kind.description: The kind of the item this one waits for (`meter`).

live_id.description: The live item: the one with the same `external_id`, or the one the write created (in a dry run an id that is never stored). Null when there is none.

result.description: One of `created`, `updated`, `unchanged`, `needs_key`, `conflict`, `failed`, `blocked`, `not_written`. More values may be added. The real run writes only `created`, `updated` and `unchanged` items. `not_written` is an item this run could write but didn't, with the reason in `error.code`: `archived_not_in_live` (archived in test, and live has no item with its key), `promote_check_failed` (the check failed for another item and `force` wasn't sent), `changed_since_check` (its write isn't the one the run checked; promote again).

write_result.description: On `created`, `updated` and `unchanged`: the `write_result` of the item’s upsert (`POST /v1/products`, `POST /v1/meters`), with promote’s warnings: `reference_planned` for a usage price naming a meter the same promote creates, `possible_rename` for a keyed item without a live match that has same-name live items (see `candidates`), `feature_type_not_promoted` for product features promote doesn’t copy yet (`file`).

candidates.description: On `needs_key`, and on a keyed item without a live match (`possible_rename`): live items of the same kind with the same name (ignoring case and spacing) that no test item is paired with, ranked: same billing type first, then active before archived, then closest price. Never preselected.

proposed_external_id.description: On `needs_key` for an item without `external_id`: the test item’s id, the key to propose when no candidate with a key is picked.

feature_candidates.description: On `needs_key` for a matched product: its test features that need the same `external_id` on both sides before promote writes the product.

blocked_by.description: On `blocked`: the item it depends on.

scope.description: `selection`: every write was checked in one rolled-back transaction. `per_layer`: the selection is above the batch limit, so each dependency layer (meters, then products) was checked on its own, in batches of the limit; a usage price naming a meter of another batch is then checked as a reference by key only, and a meter test archived is checked in the batch of the products that price it in live, so a product that stops pricing it releases it first.

batches.description: How many rolled-back batches the check runs.

checked_batches.description: How many of them ran so far. The check goes on over pages within the time budget: until it equals `batches`, a page answers `next_cursor` and no items, and nothing is written.

passed.description: Whether every write passed the check; null while batches are left.

written.description: Whether the run writes: `true` when the check passed or `force` was sent; null while batches are left. When `false`, nothing was written: an item the check refused is `conflict` or `failed`, every other write `not_written` (`promote_check_failed`).

run_id.description: The run (`cprun_…`), the same on every page of it.

dry_run.description: `true` on a dry run: nothing was written.

summary.description: One count per result for this page’s items; every result always present.

items.description: This page’s items: meters, then products, then the meters test archived, each in test id order. Every item comes once per run. Empty on a page that only ran the check.

validation.description: On the real run’s first page: how its writes were checked before the first one. Null otherwise.

next_cursor.description: Send it as `cursor` with the same `select` and `dry_run` to go on; null when the run is complete.
